subject: English
passage: Archaeologists have observed similarities in the pottery, such as linear-pattern vessels, uncovered at the Bronze Age Aegean settlement of Akrotiri and those uncovered at roughly contemporaneous settlements elsewhere in the Mediterranean, including those on Crete, Cyprus, and—to a lesser extent—Sicily. Although similarities in pottery could be attributed to imitative behavior or trade, Sophia Dimitriou et al. found evidence of genetic affinity among the populations of Akrotiri, Cyprus, Crete, and Sicily.
prompt: Information in the text best supports which statement about the finding made by Dimitriou et al.?

choices.A: It raises the possibility that similarities in the design of pottery found at Bronze Age settlements in the Mediterranean emerged due to population blending between those settlements.
choices.B: It helps explain why contemporaneous Bronze Age peoples in the Mediterranean had similar pottery but lacked other obvious cultural similarities.
choices.C: It suggests that in the Bronze Age, people on Crete and Cyprus imitated pottery designs originating in Akrotiri more frequently than people in Sicily did.
choices.D: It implies that people and pottery likely arrived in Akrotiri from settlements on Cyprus and Crete at an earlier time than they did from settlements in Sicily.

explanation: Choice A is the best answer because the text indicates that Dimitriou et al. found evidence of genetic affinity among the populations of Akrotiri, Cyprus, Crete, and Sicily. Genetic affinity among populations indicates shared ancestry or interbreeding, which would occur through population movement and blending. Since the passage notes that pottery similarities could be explained by imitative behavior or trade, the discovery of genetic connections raises an alternative possibility: the similarities emerged because the populations themselves were biologically connected through migration and intermixing.
